chunks: That was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A freed slave (mawla) of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib (may Allah be pleased with him) died, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave his inheritance to the daughter of Hamza (may Allah be pleased with her).

Abu Ali said: This narration indicates that the freed slave did not have a daughter, as the general public narrate, and that a woman also inherits the Wilayah (manumission right), not as the general public believe, although they have narrated from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) like what we said.

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤِمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْعَامَّةُ: The general public (often referring to Sunnis in this context)

ai.seo_question: Does a woman inherit the Wilayah (manumission right) in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s (SAW) allocation of a freed slave’s inheritance to Hamza’s daughter, serving as a key evidence for the inheritance of *al-wala'* (manumission right) by females. Shaykh al-Tusi’s commentator, Abu Ali, contrasts this with the Sunni view that excludes females from *al-wala'*, while noting that the general public also possesses narrations from Imam Ali (AS) supporting female inheritance, suggesting a broader consensus on this specific legal point despite differing interpretations of the primary evidence.
